title: Cutover activation tooling (design section 21.12-13): CutoverAttempt reducer and daemon cutover.activate that writes the v2 activation marker - measured absent, vocabulary names only
description:
FILED BY architect-ac8532da 2026-08-28 while re-planning task-09008b4c (GA activation record) under the human's universal-unblock instruction. Prerequisite production capability for the one-way GA act; measured ABSENT symbol by symbol at HEAD 62d2eee2:
- `git grep -n CutoverAttempt HEAD -- apps packages` = 0 hits (design :243 names the aggregate with states PREVIEWED -> QUIESCE_APPROVED -> QUIESCING -> QUIESCED -> IMPORT_VERIFIED -> ACTIVATE_APPROVED -> ACTIVE | ABORTED).
- The state tuple exists ONLY as vocabulary: packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:17-18.
- `cutover.preview|quiesce|abort|activate` exist ONLY as command names: runtime-vocabulary.ts:89-90; `git grep -n '"cutover.activate"' HEAD -- apps/daemon/src` = 0 (no handler, not in any registry); runtime-error-registry.ts:159 carries a CUTOVER source for cutover.abort only.
- No `approval.decide` kind CUTOVER_ACTIVATE / CUTOVER_QUIESCE (design :1007) - 0 hits in packages/core/src and apps/daemon/src.
- No activation script under scripts/release (grep -i activat = 0). apps/daemon/src/activation/** is the FOUNDATION ATTEMPT lane - an unrelated meaning of activation; do not cite or edit it.

WHAT THE DESIGN REQUIRES (D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-rebuild-design.md :1284-1287, pinned by epic rail 1): GO_ACTIVATE is `approval.decide(CUTOVER_ACTIVATE)`, a second distinct step-up decision that binds the quiesce generation, frozen manifest, verified import head, distribution set and restore result; `cutover.activate` consumes it and ONE transaction moves ACTIVATE_APPROVED -> ACTIVE while writing the v2 activation marker/project state; only then may the first v2 authoritative command run; before it commits, `cutover.abort` unfreezes legacy; after the first v2 command no rollback is promised and legacy stays locked/readable.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS TO COMPOSE (never reimplement): core human-authority gate `checkHumanAuthority` (packages/core/src/planning/approval-authority.ts, exported at core index :248); the GO_ACTIVATE binding admission `admitActivationBinding` landed by task-09008b4c in packages/benchmark/src/activation-binding.ts (decision must be GO_ACTIVATE, exact generations bound, human grant re-checked); the restore controller's quiesce commit (task-2ff368fe) for the QUIESCED project lifecycle; the deterministic importer (task-a4593fb7) for the import head.

HUMAN SEQUENCING: the live quiesce (task-e60b874b) is deferred by the operator until the PR #3 epic closes (2026-08-27 ~17:35Z). This row is ordinary engineering and needs no human authority to BUILD, but it must not be run against the real system; every arm is store-level with fixtures, and the act itself is the successor row. Expect a SPIDR split at planning time (reducer in packages/core; handler + marker in apps/daemon; approval kind in the decide union) - the planner measures the file budget.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK first, on disk at the planner's HEAD: `admitActivationBinding` is exported from packages/benchmark/src/index.ts (task-09008b4c landed) and `git grep -n CutoverAttempt HEAD -- packages/core/src apps/daemon/src` is still EMPTY; if the admission is absent report blocked naming task-09008b4c, if a reducer already exists adopt it instead of duplicating.

A CutoverAttempt reducer in packages/core whose state tuple equals runtime-vocabulary.ts:17-18 exactly (bidirectional roster arm) and whose illegal transitions refuse with a stable code and layer; a red-first arm per legal edge and per illegal edge.

A daemon `cutover.activate` handler that consumes ONLY an admitted GO_ACTIVATE binding (admitActivationBinding) plus a human step-up decision re-checked through checkHumanAuthority, and in ONE store transaction moves ACTIVATE_APPROVED -> ACTIVE and writes the v2 activation marker; it refuses with distinct stable codes when the attempt is not ACTIVATE_APPROVED, when legacy is not QUIESCED / import not IMPORT_VERIFIED, and when any bound generation differs from the current one; a test proves no marker and no state change persists on refusal.

A test proves the first authoritative v2 command is refused before ACTIVE and accepted after, and that a GO_QUIESCE decision presented to cutover.activate refuses on decision kind; mutation drills red the transaction-atomicity and the binding-drift arms.
Standalone daemon, core and benchmark typecheck + focused tests exit 0 with nonzero count lines; every production file <=400 lines; commit by explicit pathspec; no live-system action of any kind.
taskRails: Never run any cutover step against the real legacy system in this row; fixtures and the SQLite test store only. The live act is the successor row and is human-gated.
GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE remain separate human decisions; the standing authorization (comment-c34269c9 on task-09008b4c) is not a binding and must be refused by the admission this row composes.
Compose the landed authority seams (checkHumanAuthority, admitActivationBinding); a second implementation of either is a competing authority and is forbidden.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 1 — VERIFY-OR-BLOCK GATE, EVERY PROBE ANCHORED AT A FRESHLY-CAPTURED HEAD (read-only; author no bytes). Record every command with moe.add_comment — the complete_task summary is write-only and persists nowhere.

RUN `git rev-parse HEAD` IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THE GATE AND QUOTE THAT SHA BESIDE EVERY GREP. This row was already false-blocked once by a gate anchored on a sha captured minutes earlier: worker-a224437e measured at ee36952e, which had become the PARENT rather than HEAD, and reported a genuinely-absent symbol that had landed three commits later. That block was HONEST and CORRECT AT ITS SHA — it is not a defect, it is the most common false block on this board, and it is avoided only by re-capturing HEAD at gate time. PAIR EVERY ABSENCE CLAIM WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL (`git grep -c "export" HEAD -- <same file>` exiting 0) so a zero-line result is proven rather than assumed. Run every probe UNPIPED with its own exit code; a pipe reports the tail's status.

ARCHITECT'S MEASUREMENT AT HEAD 0bf353ff — ALL FOUR PREMISES HOLD. Re-verify each; do not take these on trust.
(a) THE ADMISSION LANDED: `git grep -n "export function admitActivationBinding" HEAD -- packages/benchmark/src` -> `packages/benchmark/src/activation-binding.ts:149`, exit 0; it is re-exported from the package barrel (`git grep -c admitActivationBinding HEAD -- packages/benchmark/src/index.ts` -> 1). It arrived via commit 64ae908e ("feat(task-09008b4c): fail-closed GO_ACTIVATE binding admission and the NOT_ACTIVATED GA activation record"). Positive control on the same file returns 12 exports.
(b) THE REDUCER LANDED AND IS BARREL-REACHABLE: `git grep -n reduceCutover HEAD -- packages/core/src/index.ts` -> `:403 export { CUTOVER_COMMAND_KINDS, CUTOVER_TRANSITIONS, reduceCutover } from "./cutover/cutover-reducer.js";`. Barrel reachability is the property that matters, not file presence: core declares `exports: {".": "./src/index.ts"}`, a single subpath, so a symbol absent from that barrel is invisible to this package no matter that its own file compiles.
(c) THE DEPENDENCY EDGE IS MISSING AND IS THIS ROW'S FIRST WRITE: `apps/daemon/package.json` declares ten workspace dependencies (@moe/context, contracts, coordination, core, import, mcp, review, runner, scheduler, store) and NOT @moe/benchmark. Step 3 adds it.
(d) THE LOCK IS CLEAN RIGHT NOW: `git status --porcelain -- pnpm-lock.yaml apps/daemon/package.json` prints NOTHING. That is what makes the manifest step safe today. RE-MEASURE IT — if the lock is dirty with hunks you did not author when you get there, STOP rather than committing someone else's bytes.
(e) NOT A DUPLICATE: `git grep -n "cutover.activate" HEAD -- apps/daemon/src` is EMPTY (no handler, no registry entry). If it now hits, adopt and verify rather than building a second one.
(f) OWNERSHIP: run a file-field scan over non-DONE rows plus `git status --porcelain` on every path you will touch. NOTE A KNOWN COLLISION: `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts` is claimed by task-0ca390d9. THIS ROW ONLY READS IT and does not declare it — registration is a separate row (see the scope fence below). If you find yourself needing to EDIT it, stop: that is the successor's work.

SCOPE FENCE, decided at plan time and not the worker's to reopen. This row lands the `cutover.activate` HANDLER MODULE and the v2 activation marker. It does NOT register the kind — adding it to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, a PAYLOAD_KEYS row, the registry entry and the count consumers is a measured 10+ file fan-out, filed as task-b8272ee020a940009a11c6eb6355d578. THE ORDERING IS A SAFETY PROPERTY: an unregistered handler module is inert, while a registered kind with no handler is a decode path that accepts a command nothing serves. Handler first, registration second.

THE `checkHumanAuthority` QUESTION IS RULED (comment-56d3f5d70bdc4b8b9520c7060980e9ee) AND MUST NOT BE RE-LITIGATED. DoD-3's literal wording is unreachable: that symbol is DELIBERATELY unpublished (packages/core/src/index.ts:239 — "CURATED, NOT COMPLETE ... through `decideApprovalAuthority`, which consults it FIRST by construction") and core exposes one subpath, so a deep import fails TS6059. implementationPlan.description:
STEP 2 — THE ACTIVATION MARKER, TDD, red first. New `apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activation-marker.ts` (<=250 lines) PLUS its `.js` bridge, and its `.test.ts`. The daemon tree DOES use `.js` bridges beside every `.ts`; a missing bridge is invisible to tsc and vitest and reds unrelated files at runtime.

WHAT THE MARKER IS: the durable fact that v2 is authoritative. Design :1284-1287 — `cutover.activate` consumes the GO_ACTIVATE decision and ONE transaction moves ACTIVATE_APPROVED -> ACTIVE while writing the marker; only then may the first v2 authoritative command run; before it commits `cutover.abort` unfreezes legacy; AFTER the first v2 command no rollback is promised. Read those lines yourself (epic rail 1 pins the design file read-only) and quote them into the step note.

The module owns the marker's SHAPE and its refusals and nothing else — no store writes, no transaction, no authority. Export a frozen record type carrying at minimum the bound generation digests the admission validates, the source commit, and the moment; plus a named frozen refusal-code roster with an exact nonzero count and a module-private layer constant.

REFUSAL CODES ARE CONSTRAINED BY THE ERROR REGISTRY AND A WRONG ONE FAILS SILENTLY. `createRuntimeError` (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-error-factory.ts:93-104) looks the code up and calls `sourceAccepted`; on an unknown code OR an aggregate the descriptor does not list it RETURNS `UNKNOWN_ERROR` and DOES NOT THROW. So a wrong code compiles, runs, refuses — and loses its identity while every "it refused" arm stays green. `sourceAccepted` (:79-86) checks ONLY `descriptor.validSources.includes(source.aggregate)`; the descriptor's `cmds(...)` list is NOT consulted at creation, so no registry widening is needed. Exactly two entries admit `srcs("CUTOVER")`: `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION` (runtime-error-registry.ts:106-109, details keys aggregateKind/commandKind/sourceState) and `CUTOVER_STATE_INVALID` (:158-159, key sourceState). `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` does NOT admit CUTOVER. Confine yourself to what the registry admits and DO NOT widen it — it is a frozen roster with generated consumers.

ARMS: a well-formed marker composes; each refusal asserts its EXACT code AND layer; and a DEDICATED ARM asserts that no refusal this module produces has code `UNKNOWN_ERROR`. That arm catches the silent degradation, and step 5 drills it.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 3 — THE DEPENDENCY EDGE, THEN THE HANDLER. TDD, red first.

(A) THE EDGE FIRST, because nothing below compiles without it. `apps/daemon/package.json` declares ten workspace deps and NOT `@moe/benchmark`. Add `"@moe/benchmark": "workspace:*"` copying the exact specifier form its siblings use, then run `pnpm install --prefer-offline` ONCE from the repo root. Both `apps/daemon/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are OWNED PATHS for this row.
THE LOCK GATE, and it is NOT byte-minimality — pnpm normalizes the lockfile on ANY install, so a repo whose lock was written by a different pnpm always emits incidental peer/snapshot hunks and a "only my hunk" clause is unsatisfiable (ruled on task-09008b4c, comment-f256c27fab9a46d7b2b0c768fb012a6f). The gate is NOTHING RE-RESOLVED: `git diff -U0 -- pnpm-lock.yaml | grep -E "^[+-].*(resolution:|version: [0-9])"` must be EMPTY — anything printed is a real re-resolution and a HARD STOP. Confirm the importer landed: `grep -n -A 6 "apps/daemon:" pnpm-lock.yaml` shows @moe/benchmark with `specifier: workspace:*`, `version: link:../../packages/benchmark`. Disclose the full `git diff --stat -- pnpm-lock.yaml` and any incidental hunks verbatim in a row comment as pnpm-version normalization. If the lock was ALREADY dirty when you arrived with hunks you did not author, STOP and report rather than committing them.
PROVE THE EDGE with a compiled probe INSIDE apps/daemon importing `admitActivationBinding` from the BARE specifier, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0, probe deleted in the same command, `git status --porcelain apps/daemon/src` printing nothing after.

(B) THE HANDLER. New `apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activate-service.ts` (<=250 lines) PLUS its `.js` bridge and `.test.ts`. Export the handler in the house shape (`goal-services.ts` `GOAL_HANDLERS` is the pattern) but DO NOT add it to any handler table — registration is task-b8272ee0. Nothing imports it yet and that is correct for this row.
THE AUTHORITY CHAIN, composed and never reimplemented (task rail 3: a second implementation of either seam is a competing authority and is forbidden):
1. `admitActivationBinding(record)` from `@moe/benchmark` by bare specifier — the ONLY admission. Its refusal passes through with ITS code and layer unchanged; do not translate it and do not re-validate what it already validated.
2. The human grant re-checked through `decideApprovalAuthority` from `@moe/core` per step 1's ruling — never `checkHumanAuthority`, never a deep import. Pass the admitted grant as the `gate`; assert in an arm that the forwarded refusal carries the GATE layer, so a gate refusal is distinguishable from a policy refusal. An arm asserting only "it refused" is inadmissible — both branches refuse, and that is the identical-fence hazard.
3. `reduceCutover` from `@moe/core` (barrel line :403) for the ACTIVATE_APPROVED -> ACTIVE transition. The reducer owns which edges are legal; the handler owns authority and durability. Do NOT re-encode the edge table here.
REFUSALS, each with a distinct stable code asserted by code AND layer AND refusedBy: the attempt is not ACTIVATE_APPROVED; legacy is not QUIESCED or the import is not IMPORT_VERIFIED; any bound generation differs from the current one. On EVERY refusal assert ZERO events and NO marker persisted — that is DoD-3's fail-closed property and the arm a grader reads first.

STEP 4 — ATOMICITY, over file-backed SQLite. DoD-3 says ONE store transaction moves ACTIVATE_APPROVED -> ACTIVE **and** writes the marker. Two sequential commits are not that, and the difference is only visible after a crash.

COMPOSE THE PROVEN MULTI-LEG SEAM, do not invent one: `commitAcceptedLegs` at `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:352` takes `(store, request, plan, extraLegs)` and builds LEGS[0] from `plan` exactly as the single-leg path does, appending the extras inside ONE `commitExpectedVersionDecision`. Three production call sites already do this — `planning/approval-activation.ts:179` (whose comment at :171-176 states the discipline verbatim: LEGS[0] STAYS THE PRIMARY), `planning/graph-activation-service.ts:217`, `planning/graph-supersede-service.ts:145`. Copy that shape; do not reach past the wrapper into the store's multi-leg method without measuring why the wrapper does not fit.

ARMS over `SqliteEventStore.openForProject(databasePath, projectId)` — the shared ephemeral `openStore()` cannot express close-and-reopen. Windows kills the vitest worker on a held handle, so CLOSE before every reopen and on every failure path.
(1) ATOMICITY: inject a failure on the SECOND leg and assert, AFTER CLOSE-AND-REOPEN, that BOTH aggregate versions AND BOTH raw event cardinalities are unchanged. An arm asserting only that the call returned an error is INADMISSIBLE — it cannot tell a refused commit from a half-written one, which is the entire property this step establishes. DIVERGENCE: state which other fences the fixture crosses (admission, gate, reducer, generation checks) and why none answers first; if loosening the injection by one leaves the arm green, the fixture is not isolating and that is a FINDING.
(2) SUCCESS: both advance exactly once and the marker reads back.
(3) REPLAY: identical bytes are byte-identical and add ZERO decision and ZERO event rows — assert the row COUNTS with denominators, not the disposition.
(4) DoD-4, THE FIRST v2 COMMAND: prove an authoritative v2 command is REFUSED before ACTIVE and ACCEPTED after. Name the exact command used as the probe and why it is authoritative.
(5) DoD-4, WRONG DECISION KIND: a GO_QUIESCE decision presented to `cutover.activate` refuses on decision kind with its exact code — GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE are separate human decisions (task rail 2) and the standing authorization is NOT a binding.
NO LIVE-SYSTEM ACTION OF ANY KIND: fixtures and the SQLite test store only (task rail 1). The live cutover act is task-e60b874b and is human-gated.

STEP 5 — DRILLS, GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE HANDOFF.

RESTORE PROTOCOL: every module this row creates is UNTRACKED (`??`) until commit and `git diff` is BLIND to them — empty before, during and after. Back each mutated file to `%TEMP%/b2548479-<workerId>/` BEFORE mutating, restore, then in a SEPARATE call print SHA256 of file and backup and assert both are 64 hex chars and EQUAL (two empty hashes compare equal and print match:true). Windows %TEMP%, never MSYS /tmp. `apps/daemon/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` ARE tracked, so `git diff --exit-code` is valid for those two. Confirm each mutation LANDED before rerunning; a silent no-op write reads as green.
D1 SPLIT THE TRANSACTION: replace the single `commitAcceptedLegs` with two sequential commits -> step 4 arm (1) MUST red. It is the only arm that can see it.
D2 SKIP THE ADMISSION: bypass `admitActivationBinding` and read the binding straight from the request -> the caller-cannot-choose arm reds.
D3 WRONG DECISION KIND ACCEPTED: let a GO_QUIESCE decision through -> step 4 arm (5) reds, and ONLY it.
D4 SILENT DEGRADATION: change one refusal's `source.aggregate` to a value the descriptor does not list -> the anti-UNKNOWN_ERROR arm from step 2 MUST red. The mutant compiles, runs and still refuses, which is exactly why that arm has to exist.
A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report in the row comment, never a pass to bank.

GATES — fresh, FOREGROUND, STANDALONE. Never ';'-chained (only the last command's status survives), never piped. An exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING and is UNVERIFIED.
LEG A: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — exit 0, quote the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo. Sub-second? plant one type error as a positive control, confirm red, remove, prove by SHA256 in a separate call.
LEG B: `(cd apps/daemon && pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/cutover)` — exit 0, quote BOTH count lines. The recipe matters: the root vitest include has NO `apps/**`, so a bare `pnpm test` runs ZERO daemon tests and a bare `pnpm exec vitest run <file>` from apps/daemon prints "No test files found".
LEG C: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` for attribution — the failing-path set at HEAD minus merge-base, intersected with this row's owned paths, must be EMPTY. Disclose foreign red VERBATIM with exact failing lines and paths; never edit it, never block on it. This branch carries heavy foreign WIP, so expect some.
CLEAN-CHECKOUT PROOF: after committing, `git grep -n "admitActivationBinding" HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/cutover` must be NON-EMPTY and `grep -n -A6 "apps/daemon:" pnpm-lock.yaml` must still show the @moe/benchmark importer. A worktree-only fix is refused.
LINE CAPS: `wc -l` every production file; each <=250 target, under 400 hard.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, in the step note: can a caller supply any part of the binding (it must not — name the admission as the only entry); can the marker persist on any refusal path (it must not — assert zero events on every refusal arm); is the human grant re-checked through the PUBLISHED route only; did this row register the kind anywhere (it must NOT — `git diff --stat` over bootstrap-contracts.ts, daemon-command-vocabulary.ts and daemon-command-registry.ts must be EMPTY, and bootstrap-contracts.ts is claimed by task-0ca390d9 so an edit there is also a collision); does every new `.ts` have its `.js` bridge; and can any refusal produce `UNKNOWN_ERROR`.

DURABLE HANDOFF — moe.add_comment, not the completion summary. Keep each under ~4500 chars and SPLIT rather than truncate (both surfaces cap at 5000 SILENTLY). Carry step 1's gate measurements WITH the freshly-captured HEAD sha quoted beside each grep, the lock diff disclosure, the four drill outcomes with restore hashes, Leg A/B/C exit codes and count lines, the clean-checkout greps, and the final `wc -l`. NAME THE SUCCESSOR task-b8272ee020a940009a11c6eb6355d578 and hand it the exact symbol names it must wire plus the measured count consumers it will update: bootstrap-services.test.ts:79 (`OWNED_KINDS` set-equality), daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:186 and daemon-command-registry.test.ts:310/:318 (`toHaveLength(38)` -> 39). Commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC of this row's owned paths, message BEFORE the `--` (a `-m` after `--` is parsed as a pathspec and nothing lands). Never `git add -A`, never a bare `git commit` — the index is shared and carries foreign entries.

comments.content:
BLOCK EVIDENCE + THE CARVE-OUT. architect-a69740e0, 2026-08-28, HEAD e73e3aa7. Zero bytes authored. DoD-1 commands this block verbatim: "if the admission is absent report blocked naming task-09008b4c".

=== THREE PREMISES IN THE DESCRIPTION ARE FALSE ON DISK ===
The description states them as landed. Measured:

(1) `admitActivationBinding` — ZERO HITS REPO-WIDE.
`grep -rn "admitActivationBinding" --include=*.ts .` (excluding node_modules, INCLUDING untracked) returns NOTHING. `find . -name "activation-binding*" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` returns NOTHING. The claimed file `packages/benchmark/src/activation-binding.ts` does not exist; `packages/benchmark` DOES exist but its `src/` holds only `benchmark-*` modules. The description says task-09008b4c "landed" it — that row is BLOCKED with zero steps completed, stalled at its own step 2 on a `pnpm install` that rewrote unrelated pnpm-lock entries (its blockedReason; evidence comment-38ebb157). So the admission is not merely missing: its owner is stalled on an unrelated lock problem and is not about to produce it.

(2) `checkHumanAuthority` IS NOT REACHABLE FROM A CONSUMER, and the description's line reference is wrong in a way that inverts its meaning.
It exists at `packages/core/src/planning/approval-authority.ts:171`. But `grep -n checkHumanAuthority packages/core/src/index.ts` returns exactly ONE line — :239 — and that line is a doc comment stating the OPPOSITE of the description's claim: "CURATED, NOT COMPLETE. `checkHumanAuthority` and `refuseApprovalAuthority` [are omitted] ... through `decideApprovalAuthority`, which consults it FIRST by construction". The barrel exports `grantHumanAuthority`, `decideApprovalAuthority`, `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_CODES` and `APPROVAL_AUTHORITY_LAYERS` from that module (:247, :254) and deliberately not `checkHumanAuthority`.
`packages/core/package.json` declares `exports: {".": "./src/index.ts"}` — ONE subpath. No consumer can deep-import, this repo has no tsconfig `paths` and no project references, and a deep relative import fails TS6059.
CONSEQUENCE: DoD-3's "re-checked through `checkHumanAuthority`" is unreachable from apps/daemon AND contradicts the core module's own stated design. That is a DoD clause an architect must settle, not a worker: either the handler routes through `decideApprovalAuthority` (the core's stated route, which consults the gate first by construction) or the barrel gains a new export and the "CURATED, NOT COMPLETE" comment is revised deliberately. I am not settling it here because it changes what DoD-3 means.

(3) `CutoverAttempt` is still EMPTY — `git grep -n CutoverAttempt -- packages/core/src apps/daemon/src` = 0 hits. This premise HOLDS, so the row is correctly not a duplicate.
